query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a heterogeneous grain structure with 3D twin architectures in the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will improve its load-bearing integrity by 25% while preserving its caloric performance under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
generation.intervention: Introduction of heterogeneous grain structure with 3D twin architectures through controlled thermomechanical processing
generation.conditions: Applied-field: 0-5 Tesla, Pressure-field: 0-100 MPa, Temperature: 250-350 K, Loading: Uniaxial tension
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary and twin boundary density
generation.mechanism: Enhanced grain boundary and twin boundary density will improve the alloy's resistance to cracking and increase its load-bearing integrity by providing additional pathways for stress relaxation and crack deflection
generation.predicted_outcome: 25% increase in load-bearing integrity, measured by ultimate tensile strength, and preservation of caloric performance, measured by entropy change, relative to the unchanged alloy
generation.boundary: Applied-field: 5 Tesla, Pressure-field: 100 MPa, Temperature: 350 K, Loading: 500 MPa
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in load-bearing integrity may vary depending on the specific processing conditions and resulting microstructure, and the preservation of caloric performance may be affected by the introduction of defects or changes in the alloy's magnetic properties

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled thermomechanical processing of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy to introduce heterogeneous grain structure with 3D twin architectures, followed by measurement of load-bearing integrity and caloric performance under applied-field and pressure-field operation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ultimate tensile strength of the modified alloy is not increased by at least 15% or the entropy change is decreased by more than 10% relative to the unchanged alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
